column3: Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew has a plural form of discretion.
The Hebrew says for, calls her foreign rather than forbidden, and names her palate rather than speech.
The Hebrew explicitly makes her end the subject.
The Hebrew says her steps grasp Sheol rather than lead straight to it.
The Hebrew uses lest and a leveling image; it states her tracks wander and she does not know.
The Hebrew does not attach my to sons.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew names your splendor or honor rather than vigor.
The Hebrew says your strength, and the labors are in a foreigner's house without an explicit enrich.
Life is not separately stated after your end.

I was is past, and assembly and congregation are two separately named groups.
Close to the Hebrew.
Why is not a separate Hebrew word; the springs go outside.
The Hebrew says not for strangers with you rather than explicitly shared.
Rejoice is an imperative.
The second animal is a mountain goat, not a fawn, and the final image is intoxication in her love.
The Hebrew calls her foreign rather than explicitly an adulteress and retains the intoxication image.
The Hebrew does not repeat the LORD's name in the second clause.
The final clause is passive, he will be held.
The Hebrew says he will wander rather than being passively led astray.
